description:
FILED s543e (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21) from the #1039 probe file (scratch/s543e/p3/arrstr.pl row 7).  PRE-EXISTING (the base extraction prints it too).  LOUD (stderr only; stdout and the exit status are perl's).

REPRODUCER (scratch/s543e/p3/spf.pl):
    no warnings; my @a = (1,2); my $s = sprintf("%s", @a); print "$s\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  1                         (nothing on stderr: the warning category is off)
  PCL:          1  + on STDERR: "Redundant argument in sprintf at unknown line 0."

Two faults in one line: (1) the "redundant" warning ignores `no warnings` (perl: category `redundant`, default-off unless `use warnings`); (2) its location reads `unknown line 0` although line tracking is on by default since MAIN-READY-99.

FIX SHAPE (untried): find where p-sprintf warns (grep "Redundant argument" cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) and route it through the warnings-category test the other runtime warnings use (lib/warnings.pm's `redundant` bit), and through the ONE location reader (`p-line` / `p-file` state) the die/warn messages use.  Probe `use warnings; sprintf("%s", 1, 2)` (perl warns with `at FILE line N.`) and `use warnings; no warnings 'redundant'`.
subject: LOUD: sprintf's "Redundant argument" warning ignores `no warnings` and names "unknown line 0" -- `no warnings; sprintf("%s", @a)` writes it to STDERR where perl writes nothing
triage_reason: sprintf redundant-argument warning under no warnings
